sentences.en: By you, you mean that?
sentences.zh: 你说的“你”，是指那个吗？

sentences.en: Is it wrong?
sentences.zh: 那是错的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And some of it has to do with flaws in coverage.
sentences.zh: 其中一些原因与报道中的缺陷有关。

sentences.en: Some of it has to do with the fact that it was happening in real time and what we're being told by credible scientists as opposed to others.
sentences.zh: 其中一些原因在于，这些事情是实时发生的，而我们所得到的信息是来自可信科学家与其他人所言的对比。

sentences.en: So I think we're talking about a lot of things at once.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们是在同时讨论很多事情。

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's worthwhile to kind of slow down and say, you know, some of these organizations are both superb and flawed, including my own.
sentences.zh: 值得放慢脚步说，你知道，其中一些组织既卓越又存在缺陷，包括我自己的公司在内。

sentences.en: The question is, I think, and I think this is why you've seen the rise of partisan media like my company or John's company, is because if all the errors tend toward one direction,
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于——我想这就是为什么你会看到像我公司或约翰公司这样的党派媒体崛起的原因——如果所有的错误都倾向于同一个方向，

sentences.en: then you start to question the underlying bias of the newsroom, right?
sentences.zh: 那么你就会开始质疑新闻编辑室潜在的偏见，对吧？

sentences.en: There are very few errors in favor of Donald Trump in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》中，很少有偏袒唐纳德·特朗普的错误。

sentences.en: There are very few errors in favor of the Republican Party in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》中，很少有偏袒共和党的错误。

sentences.en: Most corrections are happening in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 大多数更正都是朝着相反的方向进行的。

sentences.en: And so you have to start—
sentences.zh: 所以你必须开始——

sentences.en: Literal corrections or course corrections over time?
sentences.zh: 是字面上的更正，还是随着时间的推移进行路线修正？

sentences.en: Both.
sentences.zh: 两者都有。

sentences.en: But I think that—and that's why, you know, the recommendation that I've made for news consumers, and I say this literally on my show frequently, is that if you actually
sentences.zh: 但我认为——这就是为什么，你知道，我给新闻消费者提出的建议，我经常在我的节目中直言不讳地说，如果你真的

sentences.en: want a good way of determining what is opinion versus what is fact, what you should do is listen to both my show and John's show.
sentences.zh: 想找一种区分观点和事实的好方法，你应该做的是同时收听我的节目和约翰的节目。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 说得有道理。

sentences.en: And any place where we agree, that's the basis of fact.
sentences.zh: 我们达成一致的地方，就是事实的基础。

sentences.en: And then every place where we disagree, that's the opinion.
sentences.zh: 而我们产生分歧的地方，就是观点。

sentences.en: But what you do is very different.
sentences.zh: 但你们所做的事情非常不同。

sentences.en: You guys are informed each in your own way.
sentences.zh: 你们每个人都以自己的方式提供了信息。

sentences.en: But I don't know that you're spending all your days dug in and reporting on one issue, talking to sources, and producing that kind of journalism.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道你们是否每天都埋头于报道某个议题，与消息来源交谈，并制作那种深度新闻。

sentences.en: That's what I read the New Yorker for.
sentences.zh: 那是我读《纽约客》的原因。

sentences.en: That's quite different.
sentences.zh: 那完全不同。

sentences.en: But you said it a moment ago, without that original reporting from news organizations, that's the basis for much of what you cover.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才也说了，如果没有新闻机构的原创报道，那将是你们所报道内容的基础。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And I would just argue that every single day, thousands of stories are reported on, right?
sentences.zh: 我只想说，每天都有成千上万的故事被报道，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's the fringiest, most incendiary things that the algorithm picks up and churns out and churns out and pumps up and pumps up and pumps up.
sentences.zh: 但算法挑选出来的、反复炒作并不断推高的，往往是最边缘、最煽动性的内容。

sentences.en: And it's the algorithm, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是算法，对吧？

sentences.en: For a moment, if we consider that what's going viral is making us sick, and we can make a choice to consume what's going viral, or just take a minute, lower the temperature, and
sentences.zh: 如果我们暂时认为病毒式传播的内容正在让我们生病，我们可以选择是去消费这些病毒式内容，还是花点时间，冷静下来，

sentences.en: have open minds.
sentences.zh: 保持开放的心态。

sentences.en: Stephanie, I do want to focus on something we do have a little bit more control over than the virality of the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮，我确实想关注一些我们比算法的病毒式传播有更多控制权的事情。

sentences.en: And that, for me, means returning to the question of 2024 coverage.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这意味着回到2024年大选报道的问题上。

sentences.en: I suspect that President Trump, just to go back to his perspective, would say that MSNBC embodies, in his mind, what he's going after here, having a particularly liberal worldview,
sentences.zh: 我怀疑特朗普总统，回到他的视角来看，会说在他心目中，MSNBC体现了他所针对的目标，即拥有特别自由派的世界观，

sentences.en: and he would argue failing to convey certain realities to people.
sentences.zh: 他会认为该媒体未能向人们传达某些现实。

sentences.en: Let's take immigration.
sentences.zh: 我们以移民问题为例。

sentences.en: Where the network—I would argue that the MSNBC's coverage of immigration tends to be
sentences.zh: 该电视网——我认为MSNBC对移民的报道往往

sentences.en: pretty sympathetic to migrants.
sentences.zh: 对移民相当同情。

sentences.en: I don't know if you would disagree with that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否会不同意这一点。

sentences.en: But how are you thinking about an issue like that post-election, given how crucial immigration was to Trump's victory?
sentences.zh: 但考虑到移民问题对特朗普的胜利至关重要，你们在选后是如何看待这个问题的？

sentences.en: Do you feel like MSNBC conveyed the reality of the immigration story to America?
sentences.zh: 你觉得MSNBC向美国传达了移民故事的真相吗？

sentences.en: I absolutely believe that I did.
sentences.zh: 我绝对相信我做到了。

sentences.en: And I know that I specifically asked Kamala Harris about it.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道我专门就此询问过卡玛拉·哈里斯。

sentences.en: Use Springfield, Ohio as an example.
sentences.zh: 以俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德为例。

sentences.en: No one was eating cats and dogs in Springfield, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 在俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德，没有人吃猫狗。

sentences.en: However, Springfield, Ohio changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 然而，斯普林菲尔德确实发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: And if we don't hold space and interview people and speak to people who say, my community is
sentences.zh: 如果我们不留出空间去采访那些说“我的社区”的人，去和他们交谈，

sentences.en: different, my town is different, and immediately not call those people who are feeling those issues.
sentences.zh: “我的城镇变了”，而不立即给那些感受到这些问题的人贴上标签。

sentences.en: If we're immediate to say, well, they're xenophobic, they're raciSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我们立即说，好吧，他们是仇外者，他们是种族主义者。

sentences.en: It's easy to say that we're a nation of immigrants and we have to welcome everyone.
sentences.zh: 说我们是一个移民国家，我们必须欢迎所有人，这很容易。

sentences.en: Immigration is complicated.
sentences.zh: 移民问题很复杂。

sentences.en: I can't speak for my entire organization.
sentences.zh: 我不能代表我的整个组织发言。

sentences.en: I can say that we accurately cover the news.
sentences.zh: 我可以说我们准确地报道了新闻。

sentences.en: Now, do I think immigration is covered in a dramatic fashion on the other side?
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为移民问题在另一方被以戏剧化的方式报道了吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: My mother is a devoted Fox News watcher.
sentences.zh: 我母亲是福克斯新闻的忠实观众。

sentences.en: And you can tell my mother that a violent caravan of criminals is making their way up from Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 你可以告诉她，一支暴力的罪犯大篷车正从委内瑞拉北上。

sentences.en: And she'll believe you because she's in Park Ridge, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 她会相信你，因为她住在新泽西州的帕克里奇。

sentences.en: But when the right wing tells my mother that there's no inflation, she knows that they're
sentences.zh: 但当右翼告诉她没有通货膨胀时，她知道他们在

sentences.en: lying because she buys London Royal from ShopRite every Friday and she knows the price of it.
sentences.zh: 撒谎，因为她每周五都在ShopRite买牛奶，她知道价格。

sentences.en: So at the end of the day, you have to tell your audience the truth.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，你必须告诉你的受众真相。

sentences.en: The challenge is, if your audience has a particular bias and they don't like what you have to say, you have to be a strong enough journalist that they're going to stay with you.
sentences.zh: 挑战在于，如果你的受众有特定的偏见，而且他们不喜欢你所说的话，你必须成为一名足够强大的记者，让他们愿意留下来听。

sentences.en: So I think the challenge for good journalists is, how do you tell people a truth that they might not love, but that they accept?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为优秀记者的挑战在于，你如何告诉人们一个他们可能不喜欢，但却能接受的真相？

sentences.en: You just tell them the truth.
sentences.zh: 你只需要告诉他们真相。

sentences.en: And that's why, you know, Ben kept using the word heiress.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，你知道，本一直使用“女继承人”这个词。

sentences.en: And I don't think that these newsrooms are making heiress.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这些新闻编辑室是在制造“女继承人”。

sentences.en: I think they have agendas.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们有议程。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, the thing that a lot of these newsrooms don't understand now is they don't control the-
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，很多新闻编辑室现在不明白的一点是，他们无法控制——

sentences.en: What do you mean these newsrooms?
sentences.zh: 你说的这些新闻编辑室是指什么？

sentences.en: MSNBC, CNN, Fox News, y'all have agendas.
sentences.zh: MSNBC、CNN、福克斯新闻，你们都有议程。

sentences.en: Tell me what's happening in this newsroom.
sentences.zh: 告诉我这个新闻编辑室里发生了什么。

sentences.en: You know how I know y'all have agendas?
sentences.zh: 你知道我怎么知道你们有议程吗？

sentences.en: MSNBC, based off all the points that you just said, I conveyed those same points and
sentences.zh: MSNBC，基于你刚才说的所有观点，我传达了同样的观点，而

sentences.en: MSNBC said I was spreading MAGA messaging.
sentences.zh: MSNBC说我在传播MAGA（让美国再次伟大）的信息。

sentences.en: You may not have done that stuff, but MSNBC as a whole, we talked about this.
sentences.zh: 你可能没做过那些事，但整个MSNBC，我们讨论过这个。

sentences.en: So they have agendas.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有议程。

sentences.en: Like they have a set of programming that they want to push to a group of people.
sentences.zh: 就像他们有一套想要推销给一群人的节目安排。

sentences.en: And when they see all of these different things happening on social media or on podcasts, they're realizing, oh man, the people aren't buying into our programming.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到社交媒体或播客上发生的所有这些不同事情时，他们意识到，哦天哪，人们不买我们的账。

sentences.en: So instead of actually listening to the people, they continue to try to push their programming.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有去倾听人们的声音，而是继续试图推销他们的节目。

sentences.en: And that's why people don't trust the media.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们不信任媒体。

sentences.en: You're saying for business reasons.
sentences.zh: 你是说出于商业原因。

sentences.en: But this idea that people don't trust the media- I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但这种“人们不信任媒体”的想法——我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know what the reasons are.
sentences.zh: 我不知道原因是什么。

sentences.en: More people are consuming media today than ever have.
sentences.zh: 今天消费媒体的人比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: But I would argue that people are more engaged and more informed than I've ever seen in my life.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们比我一生中见过的任何时候都更投入、更知情。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Just filling their face non-stop.
sentences.zh: 只是不停地填鸭式获取信息。

sentences.en: We no longer live in monoculture.
sentences.zh: 我们不再生活在单一文化中。

sentences.en: Monoculture is dead.
sentences.zh: 单一文化已经死了。

sentences.en: That's why Leonardo DiCaprio can be in a movie with a superstar director and it loses $200 million.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥可以和超级导演拍一部电影，却亏损2亿美元。

sentences.en: Because people don't even know the movie's out.
sentences.zh: 因为人们甚至不知道电影上映了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We do not share the same information.
sentences.zh: 我们不再共享相同的信息。

sentences.en: We live in a thousand different realities.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一千个不同的现实中。

sentences.en: And we're even having this discussion right now, which is kind of almost two years late.
sentences.zh: 我们现在甚至还在进行这场讨论，这几乎晚了两年。

sentences.en: Because we're having like, how have podcasts disrupted media?
sentences.zh: 因为我们还在讨论“播客是如何颠覆媒体的？”

sentences.en: It's like, that was two to four years ago.
sentences.zh: 那已经是两到四年前的事了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We've already been disrupted again.
sentences.zh: 我们已经被再次颠覆了。

sentences.en: We should be talking about how AI is going to disrupt media.
sentences.zh: 我们应该讨论人工智能将如何颠覆媒体。

sentences.en: We're having an antiquated discussion about media on traditional media.
sentences.zh: 我们正在传统媒体上进行一场关于媒体的过时讨论。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And by the way, the additional...
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，额外的……

sentences.en: We're having an initiative on one of the most listened to podcasts on the planet.
sentences.zh: 我们正在这个星球上收听率最高的播客之一上进行一项倡议。

sentences.en: Well, what I would say about that specifically...
sentences.zh: 好吧，关于这一点，我想说的是……

sentences.en: Not after what Andrew said.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁说完之后就不是了。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: No, what I would say about that specifically is that you guys, part of your success is obviously your wife.
sentences.zh: 不，关于这一点，我想说的是，你们的成功部分显然归功于你的妻子。

sentences.en: Hi, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 你好，丽莎。

sentences.en: Hi, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 你好，丽莎。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you again.
sentences.zh: 很高兴再次见到你。

sentences.en: And you guys are very talented, but you also met the moment, right?
sentences.zh: 你们非常有才华，但也抓住了时机，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But right now, we live in a thousand different realities because we went from fan clubs, which is like Instagram, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们生活在一千个不同的现实中，因为我们从粉丝俱乐部（比如Instagram）转向了，对吧？

sentences.en: To TikTok.
sentences.zh: 转向了TikTok。

sentences.en: TikTok drives culture, whether you like it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论你喜不喜欢，TikTok都在驱动文化。

sentences.en: And TikTok is pure algorithm, right?
sentences.zh: 而TikTok是纯粹的算法，对吧？

sentences.en: What they did is they realized people actually don't want to follow their friends.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到人们实际上并不想关注他们的朋友。

sentences.en: They want us to feed them the most interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 他们想让我们为他们提供最有趣的东西。

sentences.en: And interesting can be low-hanging fruit.
sentences.zh: 而“有趣”可以是唾手可得的低级趣味。

sentences.en: It could be chaos.
sentences.zh: 它可以是混乱。

sentences.en: Clickable.
sentences.zh: 可点击的。

sentences.en: Clickable, right?
sentences.zh: 可点击的，对吧？

sentences.en: Once that happened, it divided us into a thousand different silos.
sentences.zh: 一旦发生这种情况，它就把我们分成了成千上万个不同的孤岛。

sentences.en: Those silos that you're now in are getting less views, right?
sentences.zh: 你现在所在的那些孤岛，浏览量正在减少，对吧？

sentences.en: So people start going, oh, shoot, my views are going away.
sentences.zh: 所以人们开始想，哦，糟糕，我的浏览量在流失。

sentences.en: Well, what do I do to get more views?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我该怎么做才能获得更多浏览量？

sentences.en: Ratchet up the dialogue, ratchet up the rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 加剧对话，加剧言辞。

sentences.en: And now you're saying the most insane stuff because only the most insane stuff crosses over completely.
sentences.zh: 现在你说的都是最疯狂的话，因为只有最疯狂的东西才能完全跨界传播。

sentences.en: Because you need to hop out of your silo to get the views you used to do.
sentences.zh: 因为你需要跳出你的孤岛来获得你曾经拥有的浏览量。

sentences.en: Other people see it and they're like, okay, now my rhetoric needs to be extreme.
sentences.zh: 其他人看到了，他们会想，好吧，现在我的言辞也需要极端一点。

sentences.en: There's a porn star that had sex with a thousand guys in a day.
sentences.zh: 有一个色情明星一天和一千个人发生了性关系。

sentences.en: You didn't need to do that back in the day.
sentences.zh: 以前你不需要那样做。

sentences.en: But that's what you need to do to cross over.
sentences.zh: 但这就是你需要做的跨界方式。

sentences.en: So what does that mean for media?
sentences.zh: 那么这对媒体意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does that mean for any political discussion?
sentences.zh: 这对任何政治讨论意味着什么？

sentences.en: Right now, the only thing that is monoculture is news, which is what you're saying, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，唯一剩下的单一文化就是新闻，这就是你所说的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the only thing that really crosses over.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一真正能跨越圈层的东西。

sentences.en: Trump is such a magnetic force to live them or hate them.
sentences.zh: 特朗普有一种磁力，让人对他又爱又恨。

sentences.en: The only way you can get people to talk about you every single day or watch your videos every single day.
sentences.zh: 这是你能让人每天谈论你，或者每天观看你视频的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Andrew, what are you saying?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，你到底想说什么？

sentences.en: You're saying a lot of things all at once.
sentences.zh: 你一下子说了太多东西。

sentences.en: But what are you saying that's prescriptive?
sentences.zh: 但你提出的建设性意见是什么？

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: Prescriptive, like what should be done?
sentences.zh: 建设性意见，比如应该做些什么？

sentences.en: What can you recommend?
sentences.zh: 你有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: Oh, you want me to tell you what should be done?
sentences.zh: 哦，你想让我告诉你应该做什么？

sentences.en: I think it's like...
sentences.zh: 我觉得就像是……

sentences.en: In your view.
sentences.zh: 在你看来。

sentences.en: Well, there's multiple things.
